intro: Count the arches: there are fifteen. You are at Koyunbaba Bridge in Çorum province, from 1489. Bayezid II threw it over the Kızılırmak, and at 250 metres it is the longest historic crossing of that river.
history: The fifteen-arched bridge that Bayezid II threw over the Kızılırmak was finished in 1489. At 250 metres it is the longest historic crossing of that river. It takes its name from Koyun Baba, whose tomb stands nearby, and local tradition says the site was chosen on his indication.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the fifteen arches and the tomb of Koyun Baba, then look closely at the ashlar structure and the inscription.
facts: Did you know? The Kızılırmak is Türkiye's longest river, and its floods carried away most of the bridges built over it. Yet Koyunbaba has stood for five hundred and thirty years. At 250 metres, this fifteen-arched bridge is the longest historic crossing of the Kızılırmak.
outro: This brings our journey at Koyunbaba Bridge to an end. Before you go, please leave the stones untouched, keep to the marked paths and carry water with you. Thank you for listening, and enjoy your visit.
